newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares up 2.63 pct in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares up 2.63 pct in selective trade.

text.p: Istanbul's stock exchange index soared 2.63 percent on Thursday in selective trade, led by flat steel producer Eregli Demir Celik, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 ended 2.63 percent or 50 points higher at 1,953.
Trade volume jumped 35.2 percent to 32.9 trillion lira from Wednesday's 24.4 trillion.
Brokers say demand for Eregli has also boosted the index.
"An amazing buying activity was observed in Eregli," said Serdar Karatepe from Polen Securities. "Eregli was up with strong demand."
An administrative court had cancelled a tender for the privatisation of Eregli on Tuesday.
"Investors think that the next tender to be opened would be the final one because the new government is very keen on privatisation," Karatepe said.
The company is still on the government's privatisation programme.
Eregli had made up 26.7 percent of total daily trade volume. Its price rose by 13.8 percent to 26,750 on Thursday and 24.4 percent in the past two days.

"Brokers were cautious because there was not much activity in the market, except state shares which have a significant effect on the index because of their high market capitalisations," Cagatay Ozdemir from Garanti Securities said.
"The sentiment might turn to negative if demand for them finishes," Ozdemir said. "I think it is time to sell."
Some brokers said Eregli shares had attracted foreign investors. But no immediate confirmation is available.

Of the 251 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 124 to 66 and 61 were stable. The IMKB Industrial jumped 2.42 percent to 1,903, the IMKB Services gained 2.10 percent to 1,941 and the IMKB Financial up by 2.38 percent to 2,065.
The highest rise was seen in the index representing the metals sector with a sharp 9.52 percent gain.

Leading active share of the session was largely state owned flat steel producer Eregli up 3,250 to 26,750, followed by oil refiner Tupras unchanged at 16,000 and state owned petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi, unchanged at 31,000.
The three made up 34.4 percent of the total volume.
